newsitem.title: FRANCE: Schneider denies it sold Spie.
newsitem.headline: Schneider denies it sold Spie.

text.p: Schneider SA denied a market rumour that it had sold its Spie-Batignolles construction unit.

"No, it's not true. I would even say, unfortunately not. It is well known that we are trying to sell Spie and there are several options we are exploring but there is no deal," a Schneider spokesman said.
Schneider shares were up 7.20 francs at 252.20 at 0930 GMT, with dealers mentioning the sale rumour.
The Schneider spokesman confirmed the company had hosted a factory visit by investors and analysts, organised by Paribas, on Wednesday.

Paribas is holding a seminar for international investors, which included a visit on Wednesday to Schneider's Le Vaudreil connector factory in Normandy. Schneider chairman Didier Pineau-Valencienne attended a dinner with the investors at the Hilton Suffren hotel in central Paris.
"Mr Pineau-Valencienne has said nothing new to the investors but perhaps his explanations have led some investors to turn positive on the share," a Schneider official said.
"He repeated that we plan to sell Spie before the end of the year. Various negotiations are under way. The end of the year, that's between December 15 and February," the official added.

According to research house Jacques Chahine Finance, financial analysts are expecting Schneider to post a 1996 earnings per share figure of 11.4 francs, rising to 14.4 francs in 1997. But these forecasts have steadily been revised down during the year.
Schneider fell in early October after its first-half results, which showed a 26.7 percent rise, came in at the bottom end of expectations.
